- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 85+ → 86+), then fails to correct downward.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model holds too much upward bias after peaks.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and too pessimistic in the medium term (7–15 days).
- Model fails to capture downward momentum after strong recent highs — often lags by 2–5 days.
- When history shows strong downward trend, model still forecasts upward or flat, especially if recent data is noisy.
- Model overreacts to recent volatility — overestimates volatility in short-term moves, then underestimates it in medium-term.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture sudden drops or spikes in true outcomes, especially in the last 5–10 days.
- Model underestimates the “tail risk” — fails to anticipate sharp drops after a spike, especially if preceded by a strong upward move.
- Model tends to “anchor” on recent high, ignoring longer-term mean or trend reversal signals.
